stimuli.text: Initial-rate data for A + B → products:
A student heats 10 g of $$\ce{CaCO3(s)}$$, which decomposes completely: $$\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$$. The $$\ce{CO2}$$ is collected at 316 K and 0.98 atm.
The decomposition of compound X was monitored at constant temperature.
A student titrates 21.0 mL of 0.12 M weak monoprotic acid HA (Ka = 1.4 \times 10^{-4}) with 0.16 M NaOH.
3.1 g of $$\ce{KNO3}$$ dissolves in 128 g of water in a coffee-cup calorimeter. The temperature falls by 2.4 °C. Assume the solution's specific heat is 4.18 J/(g·°C).

A galvanic cell is made of a Ni electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Ni^{2+}}$$ and a Cu electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$$. Standard reduction potentials: $$\ce{Ni^{2+} + 2e- -> Ni}$$ E° = -0.25 V; $$\ce{Cu^{2+} + 2e- -> Cu}$$ E° = 0.34 V.
The photoelectron spectra of C (Z = 6) and N (Z = 7) are compared.

questions.stem: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 6.2 g. The actual yield is 4.4 g. What is the percent yield?
What is the pH of a 0.005 M solution of $$\ce{HNO3}$$ at 25 °C?

options.why: Strong acids and bases ionize completely; no equilibrium is needed.
Correct. Strong acid: [H₃O⁺] equals its concentration.

questions.stem: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 13.3 g. The actual yield is 7.4 g. What is the percent yield?
Which is a physical change?

options.why: Correct. Only intermolecular forces are overcome.

questions.stem: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 0.019 mol of solute in enough water to make 290 mL of solution?
For $$\ce{A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g)}$$, K = 8.6. A mixture has [A] = 0.6 M, [B] = 0.7 M and [C] = 0.4 M. In which direction will the reaction proceed?

options.text: It is at equilibrium, because Q = K
It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 0.381
options.why: Correct. Q = [C]²/([A][B]) = 0.381, which is less than K.

options.text: It proceeds in reverse, toward reactants, because Q = 0.381
options.why: If Q is less than K, the reaction proceeds forward.

options.text: It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 0.952

questions.stem: On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 38 kJ/mol, the transition state at 102 kJ/mol and the products at 2 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Measure from the correct starting point.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 64, ΔH = -36, reverse Ea = 100 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: Which bond is the most polar?

options.why: Correct. It has the largest electronegativity difference (1.2).

questions.stem: Two buffers have the same pH, but buffer X has ten times the concentration of each component. Which is true?

options.text: Buffer X cannot resist pH changes
Buffer X has a lower pH
options.why: The ratio, and pH, are the same.

options.text: Buffer X has a greater buffer capacity
options.why: Correct. More acid and base are available to react.

questions.explanation: More acid and base are available to react.

questions.stem: Adding an inert gas to a reaction mixture at constant volume does what to the equilibrium?

options.text: Nothing; partial pressures of the reacting gases are unchanged
Shifts it toward more gas moles
Shifts it toward fewer gas moles

questions.stem: Samples of $$\ce{CO2}$$, $$\ce{CH4}$$, $$\ce{He}$$, $$\ce{N2}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: CO2 has a larger molar mass (44 g/mol).
Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.
CH4 has a larger molar mass (16 g/mol).
N2 has a larger molar mass (28 g/mol).

questions.explanation: Molar masses: CO2 44, CH4 16, He 4, N2 28.

questions.stem: What is the energy of a photon with a wavelength of 637 nm?

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

questions.stem: Is $$\ce{NH3}$$ polar or nonpolar, and why?

options.text: Nonpolar, because it has no polar bonds
options.why: Polarity depends on both bond polarity and geometry.
Containing H does not make a molecule polar.

options.text: Polar, because its bond dipoles do not cancel
Nonpolar, because its bond dipoles cancel by symmetry
options.why: Consider the molecule's shape, not only its bonds.

questions.explanation: NH3 is trigonal pyramidal; the dipoles do not cancel.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.6 mol N₂, 0.6 mol O₂ and 0.7 mol Ar at a total pressure of 4.4 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: Use the mole fraction, not moles.
The gases are not present in equal amounts.

questions.stem: Why is HI a stronger acid than HF?

options.text: F is less electronegative than I
The H–I bond is weaker and I⁻ is larger, so H⁺ is released more easily
options.why: Correct. Bond strength decreases down the group.

questions.explanation: Bond strength decreases down the group.

questions.stem: Why does increasing temperature increase reaction rate?

options.text: A larger fraction of collisions have energy at or above the activation energy

questions.stem: What volume does 0.17 mol of gas occupy at 0.361 atm and 414 K?

options.why: 22.4 L/mol applies only at 0 °C and 1 atm.
Use R = 0.08206 with atm and L.

questions.stem: Under which conditions does a real gas deviate most from ideal behavior?

options.why: Correct. Particle volume and attractions matter most.

questions.explanation: Particle volume and attractions matter most.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 6.1. In a solution at pH 7.6, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Above the pKa, the deprotonated form dominates.

questions.stem: How many valence electrons are shown in the Lewis structure of $$\ce{SO4^{2-}}$$?

options.why: Correct. Sum the valence electrons of all atoms, then add one per negative charge (subtract one per positive charge).

questions.stem: For $$\ce{2N2O5 -> 4NO2 + O2}$$, $$\ce{N2O5}$$ is consumed at 0.14 M/s. At what rate does $$\ce{NO2}$$ form?

options.why: Divide by the reactant's coefficient too.
Correct. Multiply by the coefficient ratio 4/2.

questions.stem: A reaction has ΔG° = −50 kJ/mol but does not occur noticeably at room temperature. The best explanation is:

options.text: It has a high activation energy, so it is under kinetic control
options.why: Correct. Favorable is not the same as fast.
Negative ΔG° means K greater than 1.

questions.explanation: Favorable is not the same as fast.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0192 min⁻¹. What is its half-life?
195 g of water at 82 °C is mixed with 58 g of water at 19 °C in an insulated container. What is the final temperature?

options.why: Pair each mass with its own temperature.
Correct. Heat lost = heat gained; for water alone, a mass-weighted average.

questions.stem: A reaction has K = 32. What is K for the reaction multiplied by 2?

options.why: Multiplying by n raises K to the nth power.
K is raised to a power, not multiplied.
Correct. Reverse → 1/K; multiply by n → Kⁿ.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.1 mol N₂, 0.3 mol O₂ and 0.8 mol Ar at a total pressure of 2.6 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: The gases are not present in equal amounts.
Use the mole fraction, not moles.

questions.stem: Which compound has the greater lattice energy, $$\ce{LiF}$$ or $$\ce{BaO}$$?

options.text: $$\ce{BaO}$$, because its ions have larger charges
options.why: Correct. By Coulomb's law, attraction increases with the product of the ion charges.

options.text: $$\ce{LiF}$$, because it has more atoms per formula unit
options.why: Number of atoms does not determine lattice energy.

options.text: They are equal because both are ionic
$$\ce{LiF}$$, because its ions have larger charges

questions.explanation: BaO has ion charges 2 and 2; LiF has 1 and 1.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0161 min⁻¹. What is its half-life?
Which Lewis structure is preferred when formal charges are considered?

options.text: The one with formal charges closest to zero and any negative charge on the most electronegative atom
options.why: Correct. That is the formal charge criterion.

options.text: The one with positive charge on the most electronegative atom
The one with the largest formal charges
The one with the most double bonds

questions.explanation: That is the formal charge criterion.

questions.stem: Use the bond enthalpies to estimate ΔH for $$\ce{H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl}$$.

options.why: Correct. ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).
Broken minus formed, not formed minus broken.
Bonds formed release energy: subtract them.
Multiply each bond energy by the number of bonds.

questions.stem: A mass spectrum of a sample of chlorine shows two peaks: mass 35 with relative abundance 23% and mass 37 with 77%. What is the average atomic mass of the sample?

options.why: The isotopes are not equally abundant.
Correct. Weight each isotope mass by its fractional abundance.
Pair each mass with its own abundance.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of N in $$\ce{NO3^-}$$?

options.why: Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Correct. The oxidation numbers must sum to the species' overall charge (O usually −2, H usually +1).

questions.stem: A solution has an absorbance of 0.113 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 81 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
A solution has an absorbance of 1.25 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 390 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
Which indicator is best for titrating acetic acid with NaOH (equivalence pH ≈ 8.7)?

options.why: Correct. Its range includes the equivalence pH.

questions.explanation: Its range includes the equivalence pH.

questions.stem: Why is the enthalpy of vaporization of water much larger than its enthalpy of fusion?

options.text: Vaporization separates molecules completely, overcoming all intermolecular forces

questions.stem: 88 mL of 10.3 M solution is diluted to 217 mL. What is the new concentration?

options.why: V₂ is the total final volume.

questions.stem: A 46.7 mL sample of $$\ce{H2SO4}$$ is titrated to the equivalence point with 23 mL of 0.051 M NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

questions.stem: Why is the radius of F⁻ larger than that of F?

options.text: F⁻ has an additional electron shell
The added electron increases electron–electron repulsion with the same nuclear charge
options.why: Correct. Anions are larger than their atoms.

questions.explanation: Anions are larger than their atoms.

questions.stem: 22 mL of 0.26 M weak acid HA is titrated with 0.14 M NaOH. What volume of NaOH reaches the equivalence point?

options.why: Correct. Moles of base = moles of acid.

questions.stem: For a reaction, ΔH° = 176 kJ/mol and ΔS° = 171 J/(mol·K). What is ΔG° at 806 K, and is the reaction favorable?

options.why: Convert ΔS from J to kJ.
Correct. ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, with ΔS in kJ/(mol·K).

questions.stem: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of bromine (Br, Z = 35)?

options.why: Correct. Fill orbitals in order until 35 electrons are placed.

questions.stem: When a reaction involving 0.045 mol of limiting reactant occurs in 88 g of solution (c = 4.18 J/(g·°C)), the temperature rises by 9.8 °C. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Divide by the moles of reactant.
A temperature rise means the reaction is exothermic (negative ΔH).
Correct. q(solution) = mcΔT = 3600 J; q(reaction) = −q(solution); divide by moles.

questions.stem: Calculate ΔH° for $$\ce{2CO + O2 -> 2CO2}$$. (ΔH°f of O₂ is 0.)

options.why: Correct. Σ n ΔH°f(products) − Σ n ΔH°f(reactants).
Multiply each ΔH°f by its coefficient.

questions.stem: What is the energy of a photon with a wavelength of 379 nm?

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O}$$, 46 g of $$\ce{CH4}$$ reacts with 50 g of $$\ce{O2}$$. What mass of $$\ce{CO2}$$ can form?

options.why: Not all of both reactants reacts.
Apply the mole ratio from the equation.
Use the limiting reactant, which gives less product.
Correct. O2 is the limiting reactant.

questions.stem: A photoelectron spectrum shows 6 peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative heights are 2 : 2 : 6 : 2 : 6 : 1. Which element is it?

options.why: Correct. The peaks correspond to $$1s^{2}\,2s^{2}\,2p^{6}\,3s^{2}\,3p^{6}\,4s^{1}$$, which has 19 electrons.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.5 M solution of acetic acid (Ka = 1.8 \times 10^{-5})?

options.why: Correct. Solve Ka = x²/(C − x) for x = [H₃O⁺].
A weak acid does not ionize completely.

questions.stem: The Ksp of $$\ce{AgBr}$$ is 5 \times 10^{-13}. What is its molar solubility in pure water?

options.why: This salt gives two ions: Ksp = s².

questions.stem: What is E°cell for a galvanic cell made from these half-cells?

options.why: Cathode minus anode; a galvanic cell is positive.
E° does not change when half-reactions are multiplied.

questions.stem: What is the rate law?

options.why: Correct. Doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 1; doubling [B] multiplies it by 1.
Recheck how the rate changes when [B] doubles.
Recheck how the rate changes when [A] doubles.
Orders are found from the data, not from coefficients.

questions.explanation: Trials 1→2: rate ×1, so order 0 in A. Trials 1→3: rate ×1, so order 0 in B.

questions.stem: Reaction 1 has ΔH₁ = -99 kJ and reaction 2 has ΔH₂ = -67 kJ. A target reaction is obtained by doubling reaction 1 and adding reaction 2. What is ΔH for the target reaction?

options.why: Reversing changes the sign of ΔH₂.
Correct. Reverse → change sign; multiply → multiply ΔH; then add.
Enthalpies add; they do not multiply.

questions.stem: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 0.129 mol of solute in enough water to make 972 mL of solution?
A compound (dinitrogen tetroxide) is 30.4% N, 69.6% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?

options.why: That is the molecular formula; reduce to the simplest ratio.
Correct. Convert each percent (in 100 g) to moles and divide by the smallest.

questions.explanation: The mole ratio reduces to NO2; the molecular formula is N2O4.

questions.stem: The Ksp of $$\ce{AgBr}$$ is 5 \times 10^{-13}. What is its molar solubility in a solution that already contains 0.1 M of its anion?

options.why: The common ion's concentration dominates; no square root.
That is the solubility in pure water.
Correct. Ksp = s(c), so s = Ksp/c.

questions.stem: A reaction has ΔH° = -22 kJ/mol and ΔS° = -216 J/(mol·K). Below what temperature is it thermodynamically favorable?

options.why: Correct. Set ΔG = 0: T = ΔH/ΔS (with ΔH in J).
Convert ΔH to J (or ΔS to kJ).

questions.stem: The first four ionization energies of an element are 686, 5488, 8726, 12914 kJ/mol. In which group of the periodic table is the element most likely found?

options.why: Correct. The large jump comes after removing 1 electron, so it has 1 valence electron.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.

questions.explanation: The big jump marks the start of removing core electrons.

questions.stem: At 298 K, ΔG° for a reaction is 17 kJ/mol. What is K?

options.why: Correct. K = e^(−ΔG°/RT), with ΔG° in J/mol and R = 8.314.

questions.explanation: ln K = -6.86; K = 1.05 \times 10^{-3}. Positive ΔG°: K less than 1.

questions.stem: A buffer contains 0.17 mol of a weak acid HA (pKa 9.25) and 0.39 mol of A⁻. What is its pH?
For $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$, initial [H₂] = 1.6 M and [I₂] = 1.6 M, with no HI. At equilibrium, [HI] = 1.54 M. What is K?

parts.prompt: Calculate the number of moles of CO₂ produced.

rubric.criterion: Correct moles using molar mass 100.09 g/mol and the 1:1 ratio.

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of CO₂ expected.
The student measures 2.274 L of gas. Calculate the percent yield, and give one experimental reason the yield could be less than 100%.

rubric.example: Incomplete decomposition (not heated long enough) or gas leaking from the apparatus.

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a complete Lewis diagram for CO₂, and identify its molecular geometry and the hybridization of carbon.

rubric.example: O=C=O with two lone pairs on each O (16 valence electrons).

parts.prompt: Explain why CO₂ is nonpolar even though C=O bonds are polar.

rubric.criterion: Linear symmetry makes the bond dipoles cancel.

parts.prompt: CaO is an ionic solid. Explain, using Coulomb's law, why CaO has a higher melting point than KCl.

rubric.criterion: Larger ion charges in CaO (2+/2−) than in KCl (1+/1−).
Greater electrostatic attraction (and smaller ions) means more energy is needed to separate the ions.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average rate of disappearance of X between 0 and 20 s.
Determine the order of the reaction with respect to X. Justify your answer using the data.

rubric.example: Equal time intervals give equal changes in 1/[X].

parts.prompt: Write the rate law and determine the rate constant, with units.
Calculate the half-life of the reaction (for the initial concentration).
A proposed mechanism has a slow first step: 2X → X₂. Is the mechanism consistent with the rate law? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Yes; the slow step's elementary rate law matches the observed rate law.

parts.prompt: A catalyst is added. Explain its effect on the rate and on the rate constant, using activation energy.

rubric.example: The catalyst provides a new pathway.

rubric.criterion: Lower activation energy means a larger fraction of collisions are successful.

parts.prompt: Write the net ionic equation for the titration reaction.
Calculate the initial pH of the acid solution.

rubric.criterion: Ka expression set up with x = [H₃O⁺].

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of NaOH needed to reach the equivalence point.
What is the pH at the half-equivalence point? Justify.
Calculate the pH at the equivalence point.

rubric.criterion: Uses Kb = Kw/Ka and the diluted [A⁻].

parts.prompt: Choose an appropriate indicator from: methyl orange (pKa 3.7), bromothymol blue (pKa 7.0), phenolphthalein (pKa 9.3). Justify.

rubric.criterion: Indicator whose pKa is closest to the equivalence pH.

parts.prompt: Explain why the solution at the half-equivalence point resists pH change when a small amount of HCl is added.

rubric.criterion: A⁻ reacts with added H⁺ to form HA (buffer).
rubric.example: A⁻ + H₃O⁺ → HA + H₂O, so the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes only slightly.

parts.prompt: Is the dissolution endothermic or exothermic? Justify.

rubric.example: Endothermic: the solution cooled, so energy was absorbed.

parts.prompt: Calculate the heat absorbed or released by the solution.
Calculate ΔH of dissolution in kJ/mol.
If some heat escaped to the surroundings, would the magnitude of the calculated ΔH be too large or too small? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Too small, because the measured temperature change is smaller than the true change.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced net ionic equation for the cell reaction.
Calculate E°cell.
Calculate ΔG° for the cell reaction.
The concentration of Ni²⁺ is increased to 2.0 M. Predict the effect on the cell potential and justify.

rubric.criterion: E decreases because Q increases (a product's concentration rises).
rubric.example: Q greater than 1 → E less than E°.

questions.title: Solubility of a slightly soluble salt

parts.prompt: Write the Ksp expression.
Calculate the molar solubility in pure water.
Calculate the molar solubility in a solution containing 0.05 M F⁻ (from a soluble salt).
Explain how lowering the pH affects the solubility.

rubric.criterion: Correct reasoning about whether the anion is basic.
rubric.example: Solubility increases: H⁺ reacts with F⁻ (a base), shifting the equilibrium toward dissolving.

parts.prompt: Write the electron configuration of N.
Explain why the 1s peak of N has a higher binding energy than the 1s peak of C.

rubric.criterion: N has more protons, so 1s electrons are attracted more strongly (Coulomb's law).

parts.prompt: Describe one difference in the number or relative height of peaks between the two spectra.

rubric.criterion: A valid difference based on configurations.
rubric.example: N has one more electron, so its outermost peak is taller or an extra peak appears.

parts.prompt: Which element has the larger atomic radius? Justify using Coulomb's law.

rubric.criterion: C: fewer protons with similar shielding, so valence electrons are held less tightly.
rubric.example: Same period; effective nuclear charge increases across.
